Zheng He was a fifteenth-century Chinese admiral and explorer who commanded massive maritime expeditions across the Indian Ocean on behalf of the Ming Dynasty. He rose from slavery to become a trusted eunuch-admiral at the court of the Yongle Emperor. Between 1405 and 1433, he commanded seven massive expeditions with fleets of over three hundred ships carrying thousands of men, tribute collectors, and scientists.

His largest vessels, the treasure ships, were reputedly over four hundred feet long—dwarfing Columbus's Santa Maria by a factor of five or more. These expeditions sailed to East Africa, the Arab Peninsula, and throughout the Indian Ocean coast, establishing Chinese prestige and gathering tribute from dozens of foreign kingdoms. Zheng He brought back exotic animals like giraffes, ostriches, and zebras, along with plants and spices. He mapped and charted routes and lands; his detailed maps influenced cartography throughout Asia and reached the Middle East, expanding Chinese geographical knowledge and demonstrating Chinese maritime power.

But after his death, the Ming Dynasty dismantled the treasure fleet and turned inward, abandoning maritime exploration entirely. Within decades, the Indian Ocean became dominated by European powers instead, reshaping the global balance of power and ceding the seas that China had once commanded.
